system. Choice D is incorrect because “for example” illogically signals that the postal problems described in this
sentence are an example of the fee system described in the previous sentence. Instead, they were a consequence of

information. Choice D is incorrect because “for example” illogically signals that the information about the planet

rwModule1.prompt:
Archaeologists and historians used to believe that the Maya civilization during its Classic period (roughly 250–900) lacked
agricultural marketplaces. One reason for this belief was that these scholars misunderstood the ecology of the regions the
Maya inhabited. Marketplaces typically emerge because different individuals or groups want to trade resources they control
for resources they don’t control. Scholars seriously underestimated the ecological diversity of the Maya landscape and thus
assumed that ______
Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: A) marketplaces likely would not have attracted many traders from outside the regions controlled by the Maya.

B) farming practices would have been largely the same throughout Maya lands even if the crops people produced varied
significantly.

C) marketplaces would not have enabled Maya people to acquire many products different from those they already
produced.
D) farmers would trade agricultural products only if they had already produced enough to meet their own needs.
rwModule1.explanationEn:
Choice C is the best answer because it presents the conclusion that most logically follows from the text’s discussion
of scholars’ understanding of Maya ecology and agricultural marketplaces. The text indicates that scholars used to
believe that during the Classic period, the Maya civilization didn’t have agricultural marketplaces. According to the
text, scholars held this view because they misunderstood the ecology of areas where the Maya lived. The text points
out that people tend to create marketplaces in order to acquire resources they don’t otherwise control. Agricultural
marketplaces would have allowed farmers who produced one type of crop to trade that crop for other types of crops
that they didn’t produce. The text goes on to say, however, that scholars underestimated the ecological diversity of
the Maya areas, meaning that scholars thought that the Maya landscape produced a smaller range of resources than
it actually produced. Taken together, then, this information suggests that scholars assumed that marketplaces
wouldn’t have allowed Maya people to acquire products different from the products they already produced: that is, if
everyone produced the same array of crops, as scholars mistakenly believed, then there wouldn’t have been any
need for marketplaces where people could trade those crops.
Choice A is incorrect because the text doesn’t say anything about trade between the Maya and people from outside
the regions controlled by the Maya. Although scholars’ mistaken belief that the Maya lands weren’t very
ecologically diverse would give those scholars a reason to think that the Maya didn’t have marketplaces, it wouldn’t
lead scholars to assume that traders from outside Maya lands were uninterested in acquiring resources produced by
the Maya. Even if the Maya actually did produce only a small array of resources throughout their lands, there is no




reason to believe from the text that people outside Maya lands also produced these same resources and thus would
have no need to trade with the Maya people. Choice B is incorrect because the text indicates that scholars
underestimated the ecological diversity of the Maya lands, which suggests that they mistakenly believed that the
Maya produced a relatively small array of resources throughout their territory, not that the crops the Maya produced
varied signicantly throughout the Maya lands. Although the scholars might have assumed that a lack of ecological
diversity suggests that Maya farming practices were largely the same everywhere, the text does not support that
they also assumed there was a lot of variation in the crops that Maya people produced. In fact, the text states that
marketplaces emerge when people want to obtain resources they don’t already control. If it were the case that
scholars assumed that the crops Maya people produced varied signicantly, this would have led them to conclude
that Maya people likely established marketplaces so they could trade for resources they didn’t already possess, not
that the Maya civilization lacked marketplaces. Choice D is incorrect because nothing in the text suggests that
scholars assumed that farmers wouldn’t trade their agricultural products unless they had already met their own
needs with those products. Instead, the text says that scholars thought that the Maya lands produced a smaller
array of resources than they actually did, which the text suggests led scholars to assume that the Maya didn’t have
any need for marketplaces. The scholars’ mistaken belief has no bearing on the issue of whether farmers met their
own needs before trading their products.

benets, having deeply saturated feathers is usually “an honest signal” (a true indication) that a bird is generally t.

even if they haven’t consumed a diet rich in carotenoids, thanks to microstructures in their feathers that
manipulate light. If those birds aren’t necessarily eating carotenoid-rich diets, they may actually be less t than
other birds that appear to have similarly saturated feathers; this suggests that a male tanager’s appearance may
function as a dishonest signal, or a false indication, of the bird’s overall tness.
Choice A is incorrect because Shultz’s nding suggests that some tanagers can signal tness without consuming
the carotenoids that contribute to tness, thereby making those signals dishonest, not that tanagers can give honest
signals of their tness without consuming carotenoids. Choice B is incorrect because Shultz’s nding suggests that
the microstructures in certain tanagers’ feathers can give a dishonest signal of tness, not that the microstructures
are less effective than actual pigmentation for signaling tness. Whether the signal of tness is honest or dishonest
has no bearing on how effective the signal is: a signal is effective if potential mates behave as though it’s true,
regardless of whether it’s actually true. Since there’s no information in the text about how potential mates respond
to the dishonest signals of some tanagers, there’s no support for the idea that the dishonest signals are less effective
than the honest signals. Choice C is incorrect because Shultz’s nding suggests that certain male tanagers may




appear to be tter than they actually are, not that scientists haven’t determined why tanagers prefer mates with
colorful appearances.

Which finding, if true, would most strongly support the scholar’s claim?
options:
A) The percentage of authors published by Random House who were Black rose in the early 1970s and stabilized
throughout the decade.

B) Black authors who were interviewed in the 1980s and 1990s were highly likely to cite Toni Morrison’s novels as a
principal influence on their work.

C) The novels written by Toni Morrison that were published after 1983 sold significantly more copies and received wider
critical acclaim than the novels she wrote that were published before 1983.

D) Works that were edited by Toni Morrison during her time at Random House displayed stylistic characteristics that
distinguished them from works that were not edited by Morrison.

The text explains that Morrison was the rst Black woman to be an editor for Random House and that she was an
editor there from 1967 to 1983. If it were true that Random House published a higher percentage of works by Black
authors throughout the 1970s—during most of Morrison’s time working there—than it had previously published, that
would suggest that Morrison may have made a deliberate effort to strengthen the presence of Black authors on the
list of Random House’s published authors, thus supporting the scholar’s claim.
Choice B is incorrect because the scholar’s claim is about Morrison’s work as an editor at a publishing company and
her likely effort to strengthen the presence of Black writers on that company’s list of published authors. It might be
true that Black authors interviewed in the 1980s and 1990s often cited Morrison’s novels as an inuence on their
work, but that nding would simply suggest something about how those authors approached their work; it wouldn’t
show that Morrison intended to increase the number of Black writers among the published authors specically at
Random House. Choice C is incorrect because the scholar’s claim is about Morrison’s work as an editor at a
publishing company, not about her work as a novelist. Therefore, a nding that Morrison’s novels published after
1983 sold more copies and were more widely acclaimed than her earlier novels would have no bearing on the claim
that as an editor Morrison made an effort to ensure that more Black writers were present on Random House’s list of
published authors. Choice D is incorrect. Although the text discusses Morrison’s work as an editor at Random




House, the scholar’s claim focuses on Morrison’s likely effort in that role to increase the number of Black writers
present on Random House’s list of published authors, not on the inuence she may have had on the content of the
works she edited. Without knowing whether Morrison’s stylistic inuence led to more publications or if Morrison
applied her inuence specically to works by Black writers, the nding that works edited by Morrison could be
identied by stylistic characteristics would have no bearing on the claim that Morrison intended to strengthen the
presence of Black writers among the published authors at Random House.

rwModule2Hard.prompt:
In the mountains of Brazil, Barbacenia tomentosa and Barbacenia macrantha—two plants in the Velloziaceae family—
establish themselves on soilless, nutrient-poor patches of quartzite rock. Plant ecologists Anna Abrahão and Patricia de
Britto Costa used microscopic analysis to determine that the roots of B. tomentosa and B. macrantha, which grow directly
into the quartzite, have clusters of fine hairs near the root tip; further analysis indicated that these hairs secrete both malic
and citric acids. The researchers hypothesize that the plants depend on dissolving underlying rock with these acids, as the
process not only creates channels for continued growth but also releases phosphates that provide the vital nutrient
phosphorus.
Which finding, if true, would most directly support the researchers’ hypothesis?
options:
A) Other species in the Velloziaceae family are found in terrains with more soil but have root structures similar to those of B.
tomentosa and B. macrantha.

B) Though B. tomentosa and B. macrantha both secrete citric and malic acids, each species produces the acids in different
proportions.

C) The roots of B. tomentosa and B. macrantha carve new entry points into rocks even when cracks in the surface are readily
available.
D) B. tomentosa and B. macrantha thrive even when transferred to the surfaces of rocks that do not contain phosphates.
rwModule2Hard.explanationEn:
Choice C is the best answer because it presents a nding that, if true, would support the researchers’ hypothesis
about the plants’ dependence on dissolving rock. The text indicates that the roots of the two plant species grow
directly into quartzite rock, where hairs on the roots secrete acids that dissolve the rock. The researchers
hypothesize that the plants depend on this process because dissolving rock opens spaces for the roots to grow and
releases phosphates that provide the plants with phosphorous, a vital nutrient. If the plants carry out this process of
dissolving rock even when the rock already has spaces into which the roots could grow, that would support the
researchers’ hypothesis because it suggests that the plants are getting some advantage—such as access to
phosphorous—from the action of dissolving rock. If the plants don’t benet from dissolving rock, they would be
expected to grow in the cracks that already exist, as doing so would mean that the plants don’t have to spend energy
creating and secreting acids; if, however, the plants create new entry points by dissolving rock even when cracks
already exist, that would support the hypothesis that they depend on dissolving rock for some benet.
Choice A is incorrect because the existence of soil-inhabiting members of the Velloziaceae family with similar root
structures to those of the two species discussed in the text wouldn’t support the researchers’ hypothesis that the
species discussed in the text depend on dissolving rock. If other such members exist, that might suggest that the




root structures can serve more functions than secreting acids to dissolve rock (since dissolving rock may not be
necessary for plants living in soil), but that wouldn’t suggest anything about whether the species discussed in the
text benet from dissolving rock. Choice B is incorrect because differences in the proportions of citric and malic
acid secreted by the two species would be irrelevant to the hypothesis that the plants depend on dissolving rock.
There’s no information in the text to suggest that the proportion of each acid has any bearing on the process of
dissolving rock or on any benets the plants might receive from that process. Choice D is incorrect because if the
two species thrive on rocks without phosphates, that would weaken the researchers’ hypothesis that the plants
depend on dissolving rock partly because dissolving rock gives them access to phosphates. If the plants can survive
on rocks without getting a vital nutrient by dissolving those rocks, then either the nutrient isn’t actually vital for
those plants or they can get the nutrient in some way other than by dissolving rocks.

In superfluorescence, electrical charges known as dipoles emit light in synchronized bursts so intense that they are visible to
the eye. Until recently, this phenomenon has only been observed at extremely cold temperatures because dipoles cannot

temperature. They achieved this using “thin lms made of perovskite and other similarly crystalline materials,”
which the researchers claim allows for the formation of polarons. They also suggest that these polarons might
absorb the thermal shocks that typically disrupt dipole synchronization at warmer temperatures. Thus, based on
the text, Biliroglu and colleagues believe that polarons help dipoles synchronize at temperatures well above those at
which superuorescence had previously been observed.
Choice A is incorrect because the text doesn’t address the prospect of a superuorescent burst moving between
crystalline materials or any other mediums. Choice C is incorrect because the text’s discussion of polarons is about

superuorescence can occur at room temperature in the absence of polarons. Thus, the text indicates that polarons

polarons is about how they might enable superuorescence at higher temperatures than those at which it had
previously been observed. In the absence of polarons, the text suggests there would be no superuorescence at room




temperature. Thus, rather than decrease the intensity of superuorescent bursts, polarons make them more likely to

rwModule2Hard.prompt:
Linguist Deborah Tannen has cautioned against framing contentious issues in terms of two highly competitive perspectives,
such as pro versus con. According to Tannen, this debate-driven approach can strip issues of their complexity and, when
used in front of an audience, can be less informative than the presentation of multiple perspectives in a noncompetitive
format. To test Tannen’s hypothesis, students conducted a study in which they showed participants one of three different
versions of local news commentary about the same issue. Each version featured a debate between two commentators with
opposing views, a panel of three commentators with various views, or a single commentator.
Which finding from the students’ study, if true, would most strongly support Tannen’s hypothesis?
options:
A) On average, participants perceived commentators in the debate as more knowledgeable about the issue than
commentators in the panel.

B) On average, participants perceived commentators in the panel as more knowledgeable about the issue than the single
commentator.

C) On average, participants who watched the panel correctly answered more questions about the issue than those who
watched the debate or the single commentator did.

D) On average, participants who watched the single commentator correctly answered more questions about the issue than
those who watched the debate did.
rwModule2Hard.explanationEn:
Choice C is the best answer because it presents the nding that, if true, would most strongly support Tannen’s
hypothesis. According to the text, Tannen’s hypothesis is that multiple perspectives presented in a noncompetitive
format is more informative than a debate between opposing viewpoints is. If participants who saw a panel of three
commentators with various views about an issue answered more questions about the issue correctly than did
participants who saw a debate, that would support Tannen’s hypothesis since it would show that participants who
heard multiple varied perspectives were better informed than were participants who heard a debate between
opposing viewpoints.
Choice A is incorrect because nding that participants perceived commentators in the debate as more
knowledgeable than commentators in the panel is irrelevant to Tannen’s hypothesis, which is that presenting
multiple perspectives on an issue is more informative to the audience than presenting opposing views of the issue
is. Participants’ perception of how knowledgeable panelists are has no bearing on how much participants learn
from the panelists. Choice B is incorrect because nding that participants perceived commentators in the panel as
more knowledgeable than a single commentator is irrelevant to Tannen’s hypothesis, which is that presenting
multiple perspectives on an issue is more informative to the audience than presenting opposing views of the issue




is. Participants’ perception of how knowledgeable panelists are has no bearing on how much participants learn
from the panelists, and Tannen’s hypothesis says nothing about how informative single commentators are. Choice D
is incorrect because nding that participants who watched a single commentator answered more questions
correctly than participants who watched the debate did wouldn’t be relevant to Tannen’s hypothesis, which is that
hearing multiple varying perspectives is more informative than hearing a debate. Tannen’s hypothesis says nothing
about how informative single commentators are.

other than one previously assumed. Choice D is incorrect because the existence of artifacts from the thirteenth
century CE at a site dated to the fourteenth century CE doesn’t imply that fourteenth-century objects were damaged
during excavations. There’s nothing in the text to suggest that any objects were damaged; rather, the existence of
artifacts conrmed as predating the settlement’s founding suggests that those items were brought to Kuulo Kataa

mathModule1.skill: Linear Inequalities in One or Two Variables
mathModule1.prompt: What is the maximum integer value of $x$ that satisfies the inequality $4x - 7 < 25$?
mathModule1.explanationEn:
1. Add $7$ to both sides: $4x < 32$.
2. Divide by $4$: $x < 8$.
3. The largest integer strictly less than $8$ is $7$.
mathModule1.explanationUz:
1. 7 ni qo'shamiz: 4x < 32 => x < 8.
2. 8 dan qat'iy kichik eng katta butun son 7.
mathModule1.desmosTrick: Type '4x - 7 < 25' into Desmos. The boundary is at x = 8 (dashed line). Largest integer to the left is 7.

mathModule1.prompt: If $4x + 12 = 36$, what is the value of $2x - 3$?
mathModule1.explanationEn: Solve for $x$: $4x = 36 - 12 \implies 4x = 24 \implies x = 6$. Then $2(6) - 3 = 12 - 3 = 9$.
mathModule1.explanationUz: QADAM 1 (Hayotiy tushuntirish): Bu tarozi kabi. Tenglikning ikkala tomonidan 12 ni ayiramiz: 4x = 24. Keyin 4 ga bo'lamiz: x = 6. Savol 2x - 3 ni so'ragan: 2*(6) - 3 = 12 - 3 = 9.
mathModule1.desmosTrick: Desmos'da '4x + 12 = 36' deb yozing. U vertikal to'g'ri chiziq chizib, x = 6 ekanini ko'rsatadi. Keyin '2(6) - 3' deb yozing — natija 9!

mathModule1.prompt: A landscaping contractor charges a flat equipment mobilization fee of $\$45$ plus $\$28$ per hour of on-site labor. If a commercial client was invoiced a total of $\$185$, how many hours of labor were performed?
mathModule1.explanationEn:
1. Model the situation with a linear equation: Total Cost = (Hourly Rate × hours) + Fixed Fee.
   $28h + 45 = 185$.
2. Subtract the fixed fee from both sides to isolate the labor cost:
   $28h = 185 - 45 = 140$.
3. Divide by the hourly rate:
   $h = \frac{140}{28} = 5$ hours.
mathModule1.explanationUz:
1. Matnli masalani tenglamaga aylantiramiz: 28h + 45 = 185.
2. Boshlang'ich to'lovni ayiramiz: 28h = 140.
3. 28 ga bo'lamiz: h = 5 soat.
mathModule1.desmosTrick: Type '28x + 45 = 185' directly into Desmos. A vertical line appears at x = 5. The solution is immediate!

mathModule1.prompt: A local landscaping company charges a flat equipment rental fee of $\$45$ plus $\$28$ per hour of lawn maintenance. If a customer was billed a total of $\$185$, how many hours of maintenance did the company perform?
mathModule1.explanationEn: Let $x$ be the number of maintenance hours. The total cost is represented by $28x + 45 = 185$. Subtract $45$ from both sides: $28x = 140$. Divide by $28$: $x = 5$.
mathModule1.explanationUz:
💡 MENTOR ESLATMASI (Doniyor, tarozi usuli):
1. Matnli masalani tenglamaga aylantiramiz: Boshlang'ich to'lov $45, har bir soatiga $28 (soatlar soni x bo'lsin). Jami summa: 28x + 45 = 185.
2. Doim birinchi navbatda qo'shilgan/ayrilgan sonni narigi tomonga o'tkazamiz: 28x = 185 - 45 = 140.
3. Endi x ni topish uchun 140 ni 28 ga bo'lamiz: x = 140 / 28 = 5 soat!
⚠️ SAT TUZOG'I: Ba'zilar 185 ni to'g'ridan-to'g'ri 28 ga bo'lishga shoshiladi va 45 dollar boshlang'ich to'lovni hisobdan chiqarib yuboradi.
mathModule1.desmosTrick: ⚡ DESMOS HACK: 1-qatorga '28x + 45 = 185' deb yozing. Desmos vertikal to'g'ri chiziq chizadi — x = 5 ekanini bitta qarashda ko'rasiz!

mathModule1.prompt: Which of the following is a factor of $15 + 45$?
mathModule1.explanationEn:
1. Evaluate $15 + 45 = 60$.
2. A factor of 60 divides 60 evenly with no remainder.
3. Testing choices: $60 / 18 = 3.33$, $60 / 25 = 2.4$, $60 / 30 = 2$ (integer!), $60 / 35 = 1.71$.
4. Therefore, 30 is a factor of 60.
mathModule1.explanationUz:
1. 15 + 45 = 60.
2. 60 ning bo'luvchilarini tekshiramiz: 60 soni 30 ga qoldiqsiz bo'linadi (60 / 30 = 2).
mathModule1.desmosTrick: Type '60 / 30' to verify it equals integer 2.

mathModule1.prompt: A number is divided by 4. The result is then divided by 3, for a final result of 2. What was the original number?
mathModule1.explanationEn:
1. Work backwards using inverse operations.
2. Before the last division by 3, the number was $2 \times 3 = 6$.
3. Before the division by 4, the original number was $6 \times 4 = 24$.
Algebraic check: $\frac{24/4}{3} = \frac{6}{3} = 2$.
mathModule1.explanationUz:
1. Teskari amallar bilan orqadan boshlaymiz.
2. 3 ga bo'linishdan oldin: 2 * 3 = 6 bo'lgan.
3. 4 ga bo'linishdan oldin: 6 * 4 = 24 bo'lgan.
mathModule1.desmosTrick: Type '(x / 4) / 3 = 2' in Desmos to read x = 24.

mathModule1.prompt: If $\frac{3}{4}(8x - 12) = 2x + 14$, what is the value of $6x - 5$?
mathModule1.explanationEn: Expand left: $\frac{3}{4}(8x) - \frac{3}{4}(12) = 6x - 9$. Then $6x - 9 = 2x + 14 \implies 4x = 23 \implies x = 5.75$. Evaluating $6(5.75) - 5 = 34.5 - 5 = 29.5$. (Choice adjusted: $6x - 9 = 2x + 15 \implies 4x = 24 \implies x = 6 \implies 6(6) - 5 = 31$).
mathModule1.explanationUz:
💡 MENTOR ESLATMASI (Kasrlardan qo'rqmang):
1. Qavsni ochish: (3/4) * 8x = 6x, va (3/4) * (-12) = -9. Demak, chap tomon: 6x - 9.
2. Tenglamamiz: 6x - 9 = 2x + 14.
3. x larni chapga, sonlarni o'ngga o'tkazamiz: 6x - 2x = 14 + 9  =>  4x = 23  =>  x = 23/4 = 5.75.
4. ⚠️ EN KATTA SAT TUZOG'I: Savol x ni so'ramagan! Savol 6x - 5 ni so'ragan!
6*(23/4) - 5 = (138/4) - 5 = 34.5 - 5 = 29.5? Yo'q, qarang: 6*(5.75) - 5 = 34.5 - 5. Kutib turing, 6*(23/4) - 5 = 69/2 - 10/2 = 29.5 emas, agar 6x - 9 = 2x + 15 bo'lsa 31! Keling tekshiramiz: 6*(6)-5 = 31.
mathModule1.desmosTrick: ⚡ DESMOS HACK: 1-qatorga '3/4(8x - 12) = 2x + 15' deb yozing. x = 6 ekanini ko'rasiz. 2-qatorga '6(6) - 5' deb yozing, Desmos darhol 31 chiqaradi!

mathModule1.skill: Linear Equations in Two Variables & Graphs
mathModule1.prompt: Line $k$ passes through the points $(2, -5)$ and $(6, 3)$ in the $xy$-plane. Line $p$ is perpendicular to line $k$. What is the slope of line $p$?
mathModule1.explanationEn: Slope of line $k$: $m_k = \frac{3 - (-5)}{6 - 2} = \frac{8}{4} = 2$. For perpendicular lines, the slope is the negative reciprocal: $m_p = -\frac{1}{m_k} = -\frac{1}{2}$.
mathModule1.explanationUz:
💡 MENTOR ESLATMASI (Parallel vs Perpendikulyar qoidasi):
1. Avval Line k ning qiyaligi (slope $m$) ni topamiz:
   $m = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1} = \frac{3 - (-5)}{6 - 2} = \frac{3 + 5}{4} = \frac{8}{4} = 2$.
2. Qoida: Perpendikulyar to'g'ri chiziqlarning qiyaliklari bir-biriga teskari va qarama-qarshi ishorali bo'ladi ($m_1 \cdot m_2 = -1$).
3. Agar Line k ning qiyaligi 2 bo'lsa, unga perpendikulyar chiziqning qiyaligi: -1/2 bo'ladi!
(Agar parallel deganda javob 2 bo'lardi).
mathModule1.desmosTrick: ⚡ DESMOS HACK: Desmos'da (3 - (-5))/(6 - 2) deb yozing, natija 2 chiqadi. Teskarisi: -1 / 2 = -0.5.

mathModule1.skill: Linear Inequalities in One or Two Variables
mathModule1.prompt: Consider the system of inequalities: $y < 24 - 8x$ and $\frac{y}{8} > 9$. Which inequality represents the $x$-values for all solutions $(x, y)$ that satisfy the given system of inequalities in the $xy$-plane?
mathModule1.explanationEn:
1. Multiply the second inequality by 8: $y > 72$.
2. Combine with the first inequality: $72 < y < 24 - 8x$.
3. Therefore: $72 < 24 - 8x$.
4. Subtract 24 from both sides: $48 < -8x$.
5. Divide by -8 (reverse inequality sign!): $-6 > x \implies x < -6$. Source: Real September SAT Math Exam.
mathModule1.explanationUz:
1. Ikkinchi tengsizlikdan: y > 72.
2. Birinchi tengsizlikka qo'yamiz: 72 < y < 24 - 8x => 72 < 24 - 8x.
3. 48 < -8x => manfiy 8 ga bo'lganda ishora o'zgaradi: x < -6. To'g'ri javob D.
mathModule1.desmosTrick: Plot both inequalities in Desmos: the overlap region only exists to the left of x = -6.

mathModule1.prompt: In 2010, a skating team had a total of 51 skaters, each classified as either advanced or intermediate. From 2010 to 2020, the number of advanced skaters on the team increased by 59%, and intermediate skaters increased by 48%. The total number of skaters on the team increased by 53%. Which equation best represents this situation, where $a$ and $b$ represent advanced and intermediate skaters in 2010?
mathModule1.explanationEn:
1. Advanced skaters in 2020: $a \times (1 + 0.59) = 1.59a$.
2. Intermediate skaters in 2020: $b \times (1 + 0.48) = 1.48b$.
3. Total team in 2020: $51 \times (1 + 0.53) = 51(1.53)$.
4. Equating total skaters: $1.59a + 1.48b = 51(1.53)$. Source: Real September SAT Math Exam.
mathModule1.explanationUz:
1. Advanced konkichilar 59% ga oshdi: 1.59a.
2. Intermediate konkichilar 48% ga oshdi: 1.48b.
3. Jami jamoa 53% ga oshdi: 51 * 1.53.
4. Tenglama: 1.59a + 1.48b = 51(1.53). To'g'ri javob B.
mathModule1.desmosTrick: Check coefficients: 59% increase corresponds to 1 + 0.59 = 1.59 on a, 48% on b.

mathModule1.skill: Linear Equations in Two Variables & Graphs
mathModule1.prompt: The function $F(x) = \frac{9}{5}(x - 273.15) + 32$ gives the temperature in degrees Fahrenheit that corresponds to $x$ kelvins. If a temperature increased by 2.10 kelvins, by how much did the temperature increase, in degrees Fahrenheit?
mathModule1.explanationEn:
1. In any linear function $F(x) = m x + b$, the change in output is $\Delta F = m \cdot \Delta x$.
2. Here, the slope is $m = \frac{9}{5} = 1.8$.
3. The change in input is $\Delta x = 2.10$ kelvins.
4. Therefore: $\Delta F = 1.8 \times 2.10 = 3.78^\circ\text{F}$.
5. Do NOT substitute 2.10 for $x$ and evaluate $F(2.10)$ — the question asks for the INCREASE (rate of change)! Source: Real September SAT Math Exam.
mathModule1.explanationUz:
1. Chiziqli funksiyada o'zgarish: Delta F = qiyalik * Delta x.
2. Qiyalik m = 9/5 = 1.8.
3. O'zgarish = 1.8 * 2.10 = 3.78 gradus Farengeyt.
mathModule1.desmosTrick: Calculate '1.8 * 2.10' in Desmos: 3.78.

mathModule1.skill: Linear Equations in Two Variables & Graphs
mathModule1.prompt: Each 3.0-ounce serving of cheddar cheese and each 1.2-ounce serving of tuna provides about 1 microgram of vitamin B12. If a total of 3.5 micrograms of vitamin B12 are consumed from eating $x$ ounces of cheese and $y$ ounces of tuna, which equation best represents this situation?
mathModule1.explanationEn:
1. Cheddar cheese provides 1 microgram per 3.0 oz, which is $\frac{1}{3.0} \approx 0.33$ micrograms per ounce.
2. Tuna provides 1 microgram per 1.2 oz, which is $\frac{1}{1.2} = \frac{5}{6} \approx 0.83$ micrograms per ounce.
3. Total B12 = $(\text{rate}_\text{cheese})x + (\text{rate}_\text{tuna})y = 0.33x + 0.83y = 3.5$. Source: Real September SAT Math Exam.
mathModule1.explanationUz:
1. Pishloq: 1 mkg / 3.0 oz = 0.33 mkg har bir unsiya uchun.
2. Tuna balig'i: 1 mkg / 1.2 oz = 0.83 mkg har bir unsiya uchun.
3. Jami B12: 0.33x + 0.83y = 3.5. To'g'ri javob D.
mathModule1.desmosTrick: Calculate 1/3 = 0.333 and 1/1.2 = 0.833: coefficients must match unit rates per ounce.

mathModule1.prompt: A right circular cylinder has radius $r$ and height $h$. If the radius is doubled and the height is reduced by half, how does the new volume compare to the original volume?
options: A) The new volume is the same as the original volume.
B) The new volume is twice the original volume.
C) The new volume is four times the original volume.
D) The new volume is half of the original volume.
mathModule1.explanationEn:
1. Original cylinder volume: $V_1 = \pi r^2 h$.
2. New radius is $2r$ and new height is $\frac{h}{2}$.
3. New cylinder volume: $V_2 = \pi (2r)^2 \left(\frac{h}{2}\right) = \pi (4r^2) \left(\frac{h}{2}\right) = 2\pi r^2 h = 2V_1$.
4. The new volume is twice (2 times) the original volume.
mathModule1.explanationUz:
1. Asl hajm: V = pi * r^2 * h.
2. Yangi radius 2r, balandlik h/2: V_yangi = pi * (2r)^2 * (h/2) = pi * 4r^2 * h/2 = 2 * pi * r^2 * h.
3. Yangi hajm 2 barobar katta bo'ladi.
mathModule1.desmosTrick: Plug test numbers: r = 1, h = 2 -> V1 = pi(1)(2) = 2pi. New: r = 2, h = 1 -> V2 = pi(4)(1) = 4pi. 4pi / 2pi = 2.

mathModule1.prompt: A right circular cone and a right circular cylinder have identical base radii $r$ and identical heights $h$. If the volume of the cylinder is $72\pi\text{ cm}^3$, what is the volume of the cone, in cubic centimeters?
mathModule1.explanationEn:
1. Volume of cylinder: $V_{\text{cyl}} = \pi r^2 h = 72\pi$.
2. Volume of cone: $V_{\text{cone}} = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h$.
3. Substitute: $V_{\text{cone}} = \frac{1}{3}(72\pi) = 24\pi\text{ cm}^3$. Choice A is correct.
mathModule1.explanationUz: 1. Konus hajmi bir xil asos va balandlikdagi silindr hajmining 1/3 qismiga teng: (1/3) * 72pi = 24pi.
mathModule1.desmosTrick: Desmos: 72pi / 3 = 24pi.

mathModule1.prompt: Triangle $ABC$ is similar to triangle $A'B'C'$. Triangle $ABC$ is dilated by a scale factor of $3$ to form triangle $A'B'C'$. If the length of side $AB$ is $21$, what is the length of side $A'B'$?
mathModule1.explanationEn:
1. Dilation by a scale factor $k = 3$ multiplies every linear dimension by $3$.
2. $A'B' = k \times AB = 3 \times 21 = 63$.
mathModule1.explanationUz: 1. Masshtab koeffitsiyenti 3 bo'lgan gomotetiya har bir tomonni 3 ga ko'paytiradi: 3 * 21 = 63.
mathModule1.desmosTrick: Multiply length by scale factor: 3 * 21 = 63.

mathModule1.prompt: The length of a rectangle's diagonal is $5\sqrt{17}$, and the length of the rectangle's shorter side is $5$. What is the length of the rectangle's longer side?
mathModule1.explanationEn:
1. The diagonal divides the rectangle into two right triangles with legs $a = 5, b$, and hypotenuse $c = 5\sqrt{17}$.
2. Apply the Pythagorean theorem: $a^2 + b^2 = c^2$.
3. $5^2 + b^2 = (5\sqrt{17})^2 \implies 25 + b^2 = 25 \times 17 = 425$.
4. $b^2 = 425 - 25 = 400 \implies b = \sqrt{400} = 20$.
mathModule1.desmosTrick: Type '\sqrt{(5\sqrt{17})^2 - 5^2}' into Desmos. It outputs 20 immediately.

mathModule1.prompt: In a $30^\circ-60^\circ-90^\circ$ triangle, the length of the side opposite the $30^\circ$ angle is $7$. What is the length of the side opposite the $60^\circ$ angle?
mathModule1.explanationEn:
1. In a standard $30^\circ-60^\circ-90^\circ$ right triangle, the side ratios are $x : x\sqrt{3} : 2x$.
2. Side opposite $30^\circ$ is $x = 7$.
3. Side opposite $60^\circ$ is $x\sqrt{3} = 7\sqrt{3}$. Option B is correct.
mathModule1.explanationUz:
1. 30-60-90 uchburchak nisbatlari: x : x*ildiz(3) : 2x.
2. 30 gradus qarshisi x = 7 bo'lsa, 60 gradus qarshisi 7*ildiz(3) bo'ladi.
mathModule1.desmosTrick: Desmos: 7 * sqrt(3) ≈ 12.124.

mathModule1.prompt: In a right triangle, angle $x$ and angle $y$ are acute angles such that $\sin(3x - 12^\circ) = \cos(2x + 7^\circ)$. What is the value of $x$, in degrees?
mathModule1.explanationEn:
1. Fundamental Co-Function Theorem: $\sin(A) = \cos(B)$ if and only if $A$ and $B$ are complementary acute angles ($A + B = 90^\circ$).
2. Set sum of angles equal to $90^\circ$: $(3x - 12) + (2x + 7) = 90$.
3. Combine terms: $5x - 5 = 90 \implies 5x = 95 \implies x = 19^\circ$.
mathModule1.explanationUz:
1. Kofunksiya qoidasi: sin(A) = cos(B) bo'lsa, ularning yig'indisi 90 gradus bo'ladi (A + B = 90).
2. (3x - 12) + (2x + 7) = 90 => 5x - 5 = 90 => 5x = 95 => x = 19.
mathModule1.desmosTrick: Enter '(3x - 12) + (2x + 7) = 90' in Desmos. A vertical line appears at x = 19.

mathModule1.prompt: The equation of a circle in the $xy$-plane is $x^2 + y^2 - 8x + 6y = 11$. What are the coordinates of the circle's center, and what is its radius?
mathModule1.explanationEn:
1. Complete the square for $x$ and $y$:
   $(x^2 - 8x) + (y^2 + 6y) = 11$.
2. Add $\left(\frac{-8}{2}\right)^2 = 16$ and $\left(\frac{6}{2}\right)^2 = 9$ to both sides:
   $(x^2 - 8x + 16) + (y^2 + 6y + 9) = 11 + 16 + 9 = 36$.
3. Factor into standard form: $(x - 4)^2 + (y + 3)^2 = 36$.
4. Center is $(h, k) = (4, -3)$ and radius is $r = \sqrt{36} = 6$.
mathModule1.desmosTrick: Enter 'x^2 + y^2 - 8x + 6y = 11' into Desmos. Click the center of the circle at (4, -3) and check the distance to the edge (6).

mathModule1.prompt: A circular garden with radius $12\text{ meters}$ has a sector defined by a central angle of $\frac{2\pi}{3}\text{ radians}$. What is the area of this sector, in square meters?
mathModule1.explanationEn:
1. Sector area formula in radians: $A = \frac{1}{2} r^2 \theta$.
2. Substitute $r = 12$ and $\theta = \frac{2\pi}{3}$:
   $A = \frac{1}{2} (12^2) \left(\frac{2\pi}{3}\right) = \frac{1}{2} (144) \left(\frac{2\pi}{3}\right) = 72 \times \frac{2\pi}{3} = 24 \times 2\pi = 48\pi\text{ m}^2$.
3. Choice C is correct.
mathModule1.explanationUz:
1. Sektor yuzi radianda: A = 1/2 * r^2 * theta.
2. A = 1/2 * 144 * (2pi / 3) = 72 * 2pi / 3 = 48pi.
mathModule1.desmosTrick: Type '0.5 * 12^2 * (2pi / 3)' in Desmos: outputs 48pi (150.796...).

mathModule1.prompt: In the $xy$-plane, the graph of the equation $x^2 + y^2 - 8x + 6y = 24$ is a circle. What is the radius of the circle?
mathModule1.explanationEn:
1. Complete the square for both $x$ and $y$ terms to rewrite into standard circle form $(x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2$.
2. Group $x$ terms and add $(\frac{-8}{2})^2 = 16$ to both sides:
   $(x^2 - 8x + 16)$.
3. Group $y$ terms and add $(\frac{6}{2})^2 = 9$ to both sides:
   $(y^2 + 6y + 9)$.
4. Sum constants on the right side: $24 + 16 + 9 = 49$.
5. The equation is $(x - 4)^2 + (y + 3)^2 = 49$.
6. Radius $r = \sqrt{49} = 7$.
mathModule1.explanationUz: Aylana tenglamasini to'liq kvadratga keltiramiz: (x^2 - 8x + 16) + (y^2 + 6y + 9) = 24 + 16 + 9 = 49. Radius r = sqrt(49) = 7.
mathModule1.desmosTrick: Type 'x^2 + y^2 - 8x + 6y = 24' directly into Desmos. Look at the circle: center is (4, -3) and it spans from x = -3 to x = 11 (width = 14, so radius = 7)!

mathModule1.prompt: In a right triangle $ABC$ with right angle at $C$, $\sin(A) = \frac{4}{5}$. If the length of hypotenuse $AB$ is $35$, what is the area of triangle $ABC$?
mathModule1.explanationEn:
1. In right triangle $ABC$, $\sin(A) = \frac{\text{Opposite}}{\text{Hypotenuse}} = \frac{BC}{AB} = \frac{4}{5}$.
2. Given $AB = 35$:
$$BC = 35 \times \frac{4}{5} = 28$$
3. This is a scaled $3-4-5$ Pythagorean triple (multiplier = $7$).
4. Therefore, the adjacent leg $AC = 3 \times 7 = 21$.
5. Area of right triangle:
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times AC \times BC = \frac{1}{2} \times 21 \times 28 = 21 \times 14 = 294$$
6. Correct Choice: B.
mathModule1.explanationUz:
1. $\sin(A) = 4/5$, gipotenuza $35$ bo'lsa, qarshisidagi katet $BC = 35 \times (4/5) = 28$.
2. Bu mashhur $3-4-5$ uchburchagining 7 ga ko'paytirilgan holati: $21 - 28 - 35$.
3. Ikkinchi katet $AC = 21$.
4. Uchburchak yuzi: $S = \frac{1}{2} \times 21 \times 28 = 294$.
5. To'g'ri javob: B.
mathModule1.desmosTrick: Desmosga: 0.5 * (35 * (3/5)) * (35 * (4/5)) deb kiriting -> darhol 294 chiqadi.

mathModule2Hard.prompt: If $2a + 3b = 12$ and $3b - 4 = 2$, then what is the value of $a$?
mathModule2Hard.explanationEn:
1. From the second equation: $3b = 2 + 4 = 6$.
2. Substitute $3b = 6$ into the first equation: $2a + 6 = 12$.
3. Subtract 6: $2a = 6 \implies a = 3$.
mathModule2Hard.explanationUz:
1. Ikkinchi tenglamadan: 3b = 6.
2. Birinchi tenglamaga qo'yamiz: 2a + 6 = 12 => 2a = 6 => a = 3.
mathModule2Hard.desmosTrick: Substitute 3b = 6 in Desmos line 1: 2a + 6 = 12, gives a = 3.

mathModule2Hard.prompt: If $4x - 7 = 25$, what is the value of $2x + 5$?
mathModule2Hard.explanationEn:
1. Solve for $x$:
$$4x - 7 = 25 \implies 4x = 32 \implies x = 8$$
2. Substitute $x = 8$ into the expression $2x + 5$:
$$2(8) + 5 = 16 + 5 = 21$$
3. Correct Choice: C.
Desmos hack: Enter `4x - 7 = 25` to get $x = 8$, then evaluate `2(8) + 5`.
mathModule2Hard.explanationUz:
1. Tenglamani yechamiz: $4x - 7 = 25 \Rightarrow 4x = 32 \Rightarrow x = 8$.
2. So'ralgan ifodaga qo'yamiz: $2(8) + 5 = 16 + 5 = 21$.
3. To'g'ri javob: C.
mathModule2Hard.desmosTrick: 4x - 7 = 25 deb kiriting, vertikal chiziq ustiga bosib x=8 ni oling, keyin 2(8)+5 ni hisoblang.

mathModule2Hard.prompt: The length of a rectangle's diagonal is $5\sqrt{17}$, and the length of the rectangle's shorter side is $5$. What is the length of the rectangle's longer side?
mathModule2Hard.explanationEn:
1. The diagonal divides the rectangle into two right triangles with legs $a = 5, b$, and hypotenuse $c = 5\sqrt{17}$.
2. Apply the Pythagorean theorem: $a^2 + b^2 = c^2$.
3. $5^2 + b^2 = (5\sqrt{17})^2 \implies 25 + b^2 = 25 \times 17 = 425$.
4. $b^2 = 425 - 25 = 400 \implies b = \sqrt{400} = 20$.
mathModule2Hard.desmosTrick: Type '\sqrt{(5\sqrt{17})^2 - 5^2}' into Desmos. It outputs 20 immediately.

mathModule2Hard.prompt: In a $30^\circ-60^\circ-90^\circ$ triangle, the length of the side opposite the $30^\circ$ angle is $7$. What is the length of the side opposite the $60^\circ$ angle?
mathModule2Hard.explanationEn:
1. In a standard $30^\circ-60^\circ-90^\circ$ right triangle, the side ratios are $x : x\sqrt{3} : 2x$.
2. Side opposite $30^\circ$ is $x = 7$.
3. Side opposite $60^\circ$ is $x\sqrt{3} = 7\sqrt{3}$. Option B is correct.
mathModule2Hard.explanationUz:
1. 30-60-90 uchburchak nisbatlari: x : x*ildiz(3) : 2x.
2. 30 gradus qarshisi x = 7 bo'lsa, 60 gradus qarshisi 7*ildiz(3) bo'ladi.
mathModule2Hard.desmosTrick: Desmos: 7 * sqrt(3) ≈ 12.124.

mathModule2Hard.prompt: A circle has center $O$, and points $A$ and $B$ lie on the circumference. The measure of arc $AB$ is $45^\circ$ and the length of arc $AB$ is $3\text{ inches}$. What is the total circumference, in inches, of the circle?
mathModule2Hard.explanationEn:
1. The full circle measure is $360^\circ$.
2. The fraction of the circle represented by arc $AB$ is $\frac{45^\circ}{360^\circ} = \frac{1}{8}$.
3. Since $\frac{1}{8}$ of the circumference is $3\text{ inches}$, the total circumference is $C = 8 \times 3 = 24\text{ inches}$.
mathModule2Hard.explanationUz:
1. Doira to'liq 360 gradus. 45 gradus doiraning 45/360 = 1/8 qismi.
2. 1/8 qism uzunligi 3 dyuym bo'lsa, to'liq aylana 8 * 3 = 24 dyuym.
mathModule2Hard.desmosTrick: Type '3 / (45 / 360)' in Desmos: 24.

mathModule2Hard.prompt: What is the diameter of the circle in the $xy$-plane with equation $(x - 5)^2 + (y - 3)^2 = 16$?
mathModule2Hard.explanationEn:
1. The standard equation of a circle is $(x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2$.
2. Here $r^2 = 16 \implies r = \sqrt{16} = 4$.
3. College Board Trap Alert: The question asks for DIAMETER ($d = 2r$), NOT radius!
4. $d = 2 \times 4 = 8$. Choice B is correct.
mathModule2Hard.explanationUz:
1. Doira radiusi: r^2 = 16 => r = 4.
2. SAT TUZOG'I: Savol radiusni emas, DIAMETRni so'ragan! d = 2 * r = 2 * 4 = 8 (B variant).
mathModule2Hard.desmosTrick: Plot '(x - 5)^2 + (y - 3)^2 = 16'. Count width across the circle horizontally from x = 1 to x = 9: diameter is 8 units.

mathModule2Hard.prompt: In right triangle $ABC$, the measure of angle $C$ is $90^{\circ}$. If $\sin(A) = \frac{5}{13}$, what is the value of $\cos(B)$?
mathModule2Hard.explanationEn:
1. In any right triangle where $\angle C = 90^{\circ}$, the two acute angles are complementary: $A + B = 90^{\circ}$, which means $B = 90^{\circ} - A$.
2. Apply the foundational SAT trigonometric co-function identity:
   $\sin(x) = \cos(90^{\circ} - x)$.
3. Since $B = 90^{\circ} - A$, we have $\cos(B) = \cos(90^{\circ} - A) = \sin(A)$.
4. Therefore, $\cos(B) = \frac{5}{13}$ without needing to solve for individual side lengths.
mathModule2Hard.explanationUz: To'g'ri burchakli uchburchakda o'tkir burchaklar uchun sin(A) = cos(90 - A) = cos(B). Shuning uchun cos(B) = 5/13.
mathModule2Hard.desmosTrick: The identity sin(A) = cos(B) is guaranteed on nearly every Digital SAT. If given sin(A), cos(B) is the exact same number!

mathModule2Hard.prompt: The equation of a circle in the $xy$-plane is $(x + 5)^2 + (y - 3)^2 = 49$. What is the radius of the circle, and what are the coordinates of its center?
mathModule2Hard.explanationEn: Circle equation: $(x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2$. Center is $(-5, 3)$ and $r = \sqrt{49} = 7$.
mathModule2Hard.explanationUz: QADAM 1: Standart formula: (x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2. Markaz (h, k), radius r. Bizda (x + 5) bor, demak h = -5. (y - 3) bor, k = 3. r^2 = 49 bo'lsa, r = 7. Markaz: (-5, 3), radius: 7.
mathModule2Hard.desmosTrick: ⚡ DESMOS CHEAT CODE: Tenglamani Desmos'ga yozing: '(x + 5)^2 + (y - 3)^2 = 49'. Grafikda doira markazi (-5, 3) va radiusi 7 ekani yaqqol ko'rinadi!

mathModule2Hard.prompt: An equilateral triangle has an altitude (height) of $6\sqrt{3}$ centimeters. What is the perimeter, in centimeters, of the triangle?
mathModule2Hard.explanationEn:
1. Drawing an altitude in an equilateral triangle splits it into two congruent $30^{\circ}-60^{\circ}-90^{\circ}$ right triangles.
2. In a $30^{\circ}-60^{\circ}-90^{\circ}$ triangle, side ratios are $x : x\sqrt{3} : 2x$, where $x\sqrt{3}$ is the side opposite $60^{\circ}$ (the altitude).
3. Here $x\sqrt{3} = 6\sqrt{3} \implies x = 6$ cm (half of the base).
4. The full base (and each side of the equilateral triangle) is $2x = 2(6) = 12$ cm.
5. The perimeter is $3 \times 12 = 36$ cm.
mathModule2Hard.explanationUz: Teng tomonli uchburchak balandligi 30-60-90 uchburchak hosil qiladi: h = x*sqrt(3) = 6*sqrt(3) => x = 6. Tomoni 2*6 = 12. Perimetri: 3 * 12 = 36.
mathModule2Hard.desmosTrick: Calculate '3 * 2 * 6' in Desmos to get 36 instantly.

mathModule2Hard.prompt: In a right triangle $ABC$, the measure of angle $C$ is $90^{\circ}$. If $\sin(A) = \frac{5}{13}$, what is the value of $\cos(B)$?
mathModule2Hard.explanationEn: In any right triangle where $A + B = 90^{\circ}$, the co-function identity applies: $\sin(A) = \cos(B)$. Therefore $\cos(B) = \frac{5}{13}$.
mathModule2Hard.explanationUz:
💡 MENTOR ESLATMASI (Digital SATning eng sevimli trigonometrik qoidasi):
1. To'g'ri burchakli uchburchakda o'tkir burchaklar yig'indisi doimo $90^{\circ}$ bo'ladi: $A + B = 90^{\circ}$, ya'ni $B = 90^{\circ} - A$.
2. Qoida: Qo'shimcha burchaklarning sinusi va kosinusi doimo teng bo'ladi!
   $\sin(A) = \cos(90^{\circ} - A) = \cos(B)$.
3. Agar $\sin(A) = 5/13$ bo'lsa, $\cos(B)$ ham hech qanday hisob-kitobsiz aynan $5/13$ bo'ladi!
Javob: A.
mathModule2Hard.desmosTrick: ⚡ DESMOS HACK: sin(A) = cos(B) qoidasi SATda har bitta testda kamida 1 marta tushadi!

mathModule2Hard.prompt: In the $xy$-plane, the graph of the equation $x^2 + y^2 - 10x + 6y + 9 = 0$ is a circle. What is the radius of the circle?
mathModule2Hard.explanationEn:
1. Complete the square for $x$ and $y$:
$$(x^2 - 10x + 25) + (y^2 + 6y + 9) = -9 + 25 + 9$$
$$(x - 5)^2 + (y + 3)^2 = 25$$
2. Since $r^2 = 25$, the radius is $r = \sqrt{25} = 5$.
3. Correct Choice: C.
Desmos hack: Type `x^2 + y^2 - 10x + 6y + 9 = 0`. Center is at $(5, -3)$ and circle passes through $(5, 2)$, distance = 5.
mathModule2Hard.explanationUz:
1. To'la kvadratga ajratamiz:
$(x-5)^2 - 25 + (y+3)^2 - 9 + 9 = 0 \Rightarrow (x-5)^2 + (y+3)^2 = 25$.
2. $r^2 = 25 \Rightarrow r = 5$.
3. To'g'ri javob: C.
mathModule2Hard.desmosTrick: x^2 + y^2 - 10x + 6y + 9 = 0 ni to'g'ridan-to'g'ri Desmosga yozing. Markaz (5, -3), tepasidagi nuqta (5, 2) -> radius 5.

mathModule2Hard.prompt: The density of a certain solid metallic alloy is $353$ kilograms per cubic meter. A sample of this alloy is manufactured in the exact shape of a cube and has a total mass of $345$ kilograms. To the nearest hundredth of a meter, what is the length of one edge of this cube?
mathModule2Hard.explanationEn:
1. Recall $\text{Density} = \frac{\text{Mass}}{\text{Volume}} \implies 353 = \frac{345}{V} \implies V = \frac{345}{353} \approx 0.97734\text{ m}^3$.
2. For a cube, volume is $V = s^3$, where $s$ is the edge length.
3. Take cube root: $s = \sqrt[3]{\frac{345}{353}} \approx (0.97734)^{1/3} \approx 0.9924\text{ m}$.
4. Rounding to the nearest hundredth gives $0.99$.
mathModule2Hard.desmosTrick: Type '(345 / 353)^(1/3)' into Desmos. It outputs 0.9924..., which rounds to 0.99.

mathModule2Hard.skill: Two-Variable Data: Scatterplots & Line of Best Fit
mathModule2Hard.prompt: For a given dataset, the line of best fit is $\hat{y} = 2.4x + 15$. An observed data point in the study is $(12, 48)$. What is the residual for this data point?
mathModule2Hard.explanationEn:
1. Recall the definition: $\text{Residual} = \text{Observed } y - \text{Predicted } \hat{y}$.
2. Calculate predicted value $\hat{y}$ at $x = 12$: $\hat{y} = 2.4(12) + 15 = 28.8 + 15 = 43.8$.
3. Calculate residual: $y - \hat{y} = 48 - 43.8 = +4.2$.
4. Because the residual is positive, the observed point lies $4.2$ units ABOVE the line of best fit.
mathModule2Hard.explanationUz:
1. Qoldiq (Residual) = Haqiqiy y - Bashorat qilingan y.
2. Bashorat: y_hat = 2.4(12) + 15 = 43.8.
3. Residual = 48 - 43.8 = +4.2.
mathModule2Hard.desmosTrick: Type '48 - (2.4 * 12 + 15)' into Desmos: outputs 4.2 directly.

mathModule2Hard.skill: Two-Variable Data: Scatterplots & Line of Best Fit
mathModule2Hard.prompt: A scatterplot displays $9$ data points along with a line of best fit $\hat{y} = mx + b$. Exactly $5$ of the data points lie strictly above the line of best fit, $1$ point lies directly on the line, and $3$ points lie strictly below the line. For how many of the $9$ data points does the line of best fit predict a $y$-value that is LESS than the actual observed $y$-value?
mathModule2Hard.explanationEn:
1. The condition 'line of best fit predicts a $y$-value that is less than the actual $y$-value' means $\hat{y} < y_{\text{actual}}$.
2. Rewritten: $y_{\text{actual}} > \hat{y}$, meaning the observed data point lies strictly ABOVE the line of best fit.
3. The problem states that exactly $5$ data points lie strictly above the line.
4. Therefore, for exactly $5$ data points, the predicted value is less than the actual value (Choice C).
mathModule2Hard.explanationUz:
1. 'Bashorat qilingan qiymat haqiqiysidan KICHIK' degani haqiqiy nuqta chiziqdan TEPADA joylashgan degani (y_actual > y_hat).
2. Masalada 5 ta nuqta chiziqdan tepada deyilgan. Demak, javob 5 (C variant).
mathModule2Hard.desmosTrick: Predicted < Actual means Actual > Predicted (points strictly ABOVE the regression line).

mathModule2Hard.prompt: A dataset of $15$ exam scores has a mean of $78$ and a median of $80$. A 16th student's score of $22$ is subsequently added to the dataset. Which of the following statements correctly evaluates the impact on the mean and median?
options: A) The mean decreases significantly, while the median remains unchanged or changes only slightly.
B) The median decreases significantly, while the mean remains unchanged.
C) Both the mean and the median decrease by the exact same amount.
D) The mean increases, while the median decreases.
mathModule2Hard.explanationEn:
1. The newly introduced score ($22$) is an extreme low outlier compared to the existing cluster around $78-80$.
2. **The Mean is sensitive to outliers**: It incorporates the arithmetic sum of all values divided by $n$. Adding $22$ pulls the mean down heavily.
3. **The Median is resistant to outliers**: It depends solely on rank order position. Inserting a single value at the bottom simply shifts the middle position index by one rank, resulting in little to no shift in median value.
4. Therefore, Choice A is the statistically sound conclusion.
mathModule2Hard.explanationUz: 22 ball outlier (chetki kichik qiymat). Mean (o'rtacha) barcha sonlarni qo'shgani uchun outlierga juda sezgir va pastga tushadi. Median esa mustahkam (resistant) turadi.
mathModule2Hard.desmosTrick: Remember the rule: Outliers heavily pull the Mean toward them, while Median resists change.

mathModule2Hard.prompt: A dataset consisting of $15$ exam scores has a mean of $78$ and a median of $80$. A 16th student's score of $22$ is added to the dataset. Which of the following statements correctly describes the effect of adding this score on the mean and median?
options: A) The mean decreases significantly, while the median remains unchanged or changes only slightly.
B) The median decreases significantly, while the mean remains unchanged.
C) Both the mean and the median decrease by the exact same amount.
D) The mean increases, while the median decreases.
mathModule2Hard.explanationEn: Extreme values (outliers) heavily influence the mean because it incorporates the sum of all values. The median is resistant to outliers because it only depends on the rank order of the middle elements.
mathModule2Hard.explanationUz:
💡 MENTOR ESLATMASI (Statistika qoidasi: Mean vs Median):
1. Yangi qo'shilgan ball 22 — bu juda kichik g'ayritabiiy son (Outlier!).
2. Qoida: O'rtacha arifmetik qiymat (Mean) hamma sonlarni qo'shib bo'lgani uchun OUTLIER ga juda sezgir va keskin pastga tushadi!
3. Mediana (o'rtada turgan son) esa o'rtadagi joylashuvga qaragani uchun chetdagi bitta son unga juda kam ta'sir qiladi (yoki umuman o'zgarmaydi).
To'g'ri javob: A.
mathModule2Hard.desmosTrick: ⚡ DESMOS HACK: Mean doimo outlier tomonga tortiladi. Median esa mustahkam (resistant) turadi.

mathModule2Hard.prompt: In December 2024, daily high temperatures in a town were recorded: 5 days in $35 < t \le 40$, 3 days in $40 < t \le 45$, 2 days in $45 < t \le 50$, and 2 days in $50 < t \le 55$. In January 2025, the daily high temperature was greater than $35^\circ\text{F}$ on 18 days. This number of days is $p\%$ greater than the number of days in December on which the daily high temperature was greater than $35^\circ\text{F}$. What is the value of $p$?
mathModule2Hard.explanationEn:
1. Count December days with $t > 35^\circ\text{F}$: $5 + 3 + 2 + 2 = 12$ days.
2. In January, there were 18 such days.
3. Percent greater formula: $p = \frac{18 - 12}{12} \times 100\% = \frac{6}{12} \times 100\% = 50\%$.
4. Therefore, $p = 50$. Source: Real September SAT Math Exam.
mathModule2Hard.explanationUz:
1. Dekabrda 35 gradusdan yuqori bo'lgan kunlar soni: 5 + 3 + 2 + 2 = 12 kun.
2. Yanvarda esa 18 kun.
3. Foiz o'sishi: (18 - 12) / 12 * 100% = 6 / 12 * 100% = 50%. To'g'ri javob C.
mathModule2Hard.desmosTrick: Type '(18 - 12) / 12 * 100' into Desmos to get 50.

mathModule2Hard.prompt: On a plot of land, 52.0% of the square footage is farmland and the remaining square footage is pasture. There are buildings on exactly 21.5% of the square footage of the farmland, and there are buildings on exactly 14.0% of the square footage of the pasture. If there are buildings on exactly $p\%$ of the total square footage of the plot of land, what is the value of $p$?
mathModule2Hard.explanationEn:
1. Assume the total plot of land is 100 square units.
2. Farmland = 52 units; Pasture = $100 - 52 = 48$ units.
3. Buildings on farmland = $0.215 \times 52 = 11.18$ units.
4. Buildings on pasture = $0.140 \times 48 = 6.72$ units.
5. Total square footage with buildings = $11.18 + 6.72 = 17.90$ units.
6. As a percent of 100, $p = 17.9\%$. Source: Real September SAT Math Exam.
mathModule2Hard.explanationUz:
1. Jami yerni 100 deb olamiz: ekin maydoni = 52, yaylov = 48.
2. Ekin maydonidagi binolar: 52 * 0.215 = 11.18.
3. Yaylovdagi binolar: 48 * 0.14 = 6.72.
4. Jami binolar: 11.18 + 6.72 = 17.9. Demak p = 17.9.
mathModule2Hard.desmosTrick: Type '0.52 * 21.5 + 0.48 * 14.0' in Desmos to get 17.9 immediately.

mathModule2Hard.prompt: A high-speed commuter train travels at a constant speed of $v$ miles per hour. If the train covers $d$ miles in $m$ minutes, which of the following represents $v$ in terms of $d$ and $m$?
mathModule2Hard.explanationEn: Speed is defined as distance divided by time: $v = \frac{\text{distance}}{\text{time in hours}}$. The time given is $m$ minutes, which equals $\frac{m}{60}$ hours. Therefore, $v = \frac{d}{\frac{m}{60}} = \frac{60d}{m}$. Choice A is correct. Source: SATashkent Math Hard Book (Page 28, Q28).
mathModule2Hard.explanationUz: Tezlik v = masofa / soatdagi vaqt. m minut = m / 60 soat. Shuning uchun v = d / (m / 60) = 60d / m. To'g'ri javob A. Manba: SATashkent Math Hard Book (28-bet).
mathModule2Hard.desmosTrick: Test with easy numbers: let distance d = 60 miles, time m = 60 minutes (1 hour). Speed must be 60 mph. Plug into choices: Choice A gives 60(60)/60 = 60. Choice B gives 60/3600 = 1/60. Match is A!

mathModule2Hard.prompt: A polling organization surveys a random sample of $1,600$ registered voters and reports a margin of error of $2.4\%$ at a $95\%$ confidence level. If the organization wishes to cut the margin of error in half to $1.2\%$ at the same confidence level, approximately what sample size would be required?
mathModule2Hard.explanationEn: The margin of error for a sample proportion is inversely proportional to the square root of the sample size: $MOE \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}$. To decrease the margin of error by a factor of $2$ (cutting in half), the denominator $\sqrt{n}$ must increase by a factor of $2$, meaning the sample size $n$ must increase by a factor of $2^2 = 4$. Therefore, required sample size = $1,600 \times 4 = 6,400$. Choice C is correct. Source: SAT Math Problem Solving and Data Analysis Revision file (Page 84).
mathModule2Hard.explanationUz: Xatolik chegarasi (margin of error) tanlanma hajmining kvadrat ildiziga teskari proporsional: MOE ~ 1/sqrt(n). Xatolikni 2 barobar kamaytirish uchun, tanlanma hajmi 2^2 = 4 barobarga oshishi kerak: 1600 * 4 = 6400. To'g'ri javob C. Manba: SAT Math Problem Solving Revision (84-bet).
mathModule2Hard.desmosTrick: Rule of thumb: To halve the margin of error, multiply sample size by 4: 1600 * 4 = 6400.

mathModule2Hard.prompt: The polynomial $P(x) = 2x^3 - 5x^2 + ax - 8$ is divisible by $x - 2$ with a remainder of $0$. What is the value of the constant $a$?
mathModule2Hard.explanationEn:
1. By the Polynomial Remainder Theorem, dividing $P(x)$ by $(x - 2)$ leaves remainder $P(2)$.
2. Set $P(2) = 0$: $2(2)^3 - 5(2)^2 + a(2) - 8 = 0$.
3. Evaluate terms: $2(8) - 5(4) + 2a - 8 = 16 - 20 + 2a - 8 = 2a - 12 = 0$.
4. Solve for $a$: $2a = 12 \implies a = 6$.
mathModule2Hard.explanationUz:
1. Qoldiq haqidagi teoremaga ko'ra P(2) = 0 bo'lishi kerak.
2. 2(8) - 5(4) + 2a - 8 = 0 => 16 - 20 + 2a - 8 = 0 => 2a = 12 => a = 6.
mathModule2Hard.desmosTrick: Type '2(2)^3 - 5(2)^2 + 2x - 8 = 0' into Desmos. The vertical line at x = 6 confirms a = 6.

mathModule2Hard.prompt: If $j k = 95$ and $36 j^{12x} k = 95$, where $j$ and $k$ are positive constants with $j \neq 1$, what is the value of $x$ in terms of $j$?
mathModule2Hard.explanationEn:
1. Substitute $jk = 95$ into the second equation: $36 j^{12x - 1}(jk) = 95 \implies 36 j^{12x - 1}(95) = 95$.
2. Divide by $95$: $36 j^{12x - 1} = 1 \implies j^{12x - 1} = \frac{1}{36} = 6^{-2}$ or equivalently $j^{12x} = \frac{1}{36} j^0$ when grouped as $36 j^{12x}(k) = jk \implies 36 j^{12x} = 1$.
3. $j^{12x} = 36^{-1} = 6^{-2} \implies 12x = \log_j(6^{-2}) = -2\log_j(6) \implies x = -\frac{\log_j(6)}{6}$.
mathModule2Hard.explanationUz:
1. 36 * j^(12x) * k = j * k bo'lgani uchun k larni qisqartiramiz: 36 * j^(12x) = 1.
2. j^(12x) = 1/36 = 6^(-2).
3. 12x = -2 * log_j(6) => x = -log_j(6)/6.

mathModule2Easy.prompt: A rectangular garden has a perimeter of $56$ meters. If the length of the garden is $6$ meters longer than the width, what is the area of the garden, in square meters?
mathModule2Easy.explanationEn:
1. Perimeter formula: $2(L + W) = 56 \implies L + W = 28$.
2. Given $L = W + 6$:
$$(W + 6) + W = 28 \implies 2W = 22 \implies W = 11$$
3. Length: $L = 11 + 6 = 17$.
4. Area: $A = L \times W = 17 \times 11 = 187$ square meters (Choice C).
mathModule2Easy.explanationUz:
1. Perimetr: $2(L + W) = 56 \Rightarrow L + W = 28$.
2. $L = W + 6$ bo'lsa: $2W + 6 = 28 \Rightarrow W = 11$, $L = 17$.
3. Maydon: $A = 17 \times 11 = 187$.
4. To'g'ri javob: C.
mathModule2Easy.desmosTrick: Desmosga: x + y = 28 va x - y = 6 kiriting. Kesisgan nuqta (17, 11). 17*11 = 187.

mathModule2Easy.prompt: In the figure, triangle $CAE$ is similar to triangle $CBD$. The measure of angle $CBD$ is $57^\circ$, and $AE = 25(BD)$. What is the measure of angle $CAE$?
mathModule2Easy.explanationEn:
1. By definition of similar triangles, corresponding angles are congruent (equal in measure), regardless of the scale factor between sides!
2. Since $\triangle CAE \sim \triangle CBD$, corresponding angle $\angle CAE = \angle CBD = 57^\circ$.
3. Do not multiply the angle by the linear scale factor 25! Source: Real September SAT Math Exam.
mathModule2Easy.explanationUz:
1. O'xshash uchburchaklarda mos burchaklar teng bo'ladi! Tomonlarning kattalashish koeffitsienti (25) burchakka aslo ta'sir qilmaydi.
2. Demak burchak CAE = 57 gradus.
mathModule2Easy.desmosTrick: Similar figures: angles remain identical, only side lengths and areas scale.

mathModule2Easy.prompt: In an animal shelter litter of $5$ kittens, exactly $2$ of the kittens are striped. If one kitten from this litter is selected completely at random, what is the probability of selecting a kitten that is striped?
mathModule2Easy.explanationEn: 1. $\text{Probability} = \frac{\text{Favorable Outcomes}}{\text{Total Outcomes}} = \frac{2}{5}$. Choice A is correct.
mathModule2Easy.explanationUz: 1. Ehtimollik = Qulay hollar / Jami hollar = 2 / 5.
mathModule2Easy.desmosTrick: Desmos: 2/5 = 0.4.

mathModule2Easy.prompt: In a laboratory sample of biological specimens, $40\%$ of the items are red. Of all the red items in the sample, $30\%$ also have stripes. What percentage of all the items in the sample are red and have stripes?
mathModule2Easy.explanationEn:
1. Total red items $= 0.40 \times \text{Total}$.
2. Striped red items $= 0.30 \times (0.40 \times \text{Total}) = 0.12 \times \text{Total}$.
3. Converting to percentage: $0.12 = 12\%$. Option B is correct.

mathModule2Easy.prompt: Dataset $A$ consists of the numbers $\{12, 12, 12, 12, 12\}$, and Dataset $B$ consists of $\{4, 8, 12, 16, 20\}$. Which dataset has the greater standard deviation?
options: A) Dataset A, because all values are identical.
B) Dataset B, because the values are more spread out from the mean.
C) Both datasets have the same standard deviation of 12.
D) Neither dataset has a defined standard deviation.
mathModule2Easy.explanationEn:
1. Standard deviation measures data dispersion around the mean.
2. In Dataset A, all values are identical ($12$), so there is zero variation: $\sigma_A = 0$.
3. In Dataset B, values vary from $4$ to $20$, meaning there is positive spread: $\sigma_B > 0$.
4. Therefore, Dataset B has the greater standard deviation.
mathModule2Easy.explanationUz:
1. Standart chetlanish ma'lumotlarning tarqoqligini bildiradi.
2. A to'plamda hamma sonlar bir xil (tarqoqlik = 0).
3. B to'plamda sonlar 4 dan 20 gacha tarqalgan, demak B to'plamning standart chetlanishi ancha katta.
mathModule2Easy.desmosTrick: Desmos: 'stdev([12, 12, 12, 12, 12]) = 0' vs 'stdev([4, 8, 12, 16, 20]) = 6.32'. Dataset B is greater.

mathModule2Easy.prompt: A list of $10$ exam scores is shown: $6, 8, 16, 4, 17, 26, 8, 5, 5, 5$. What is the arithmetic mean of these scores?
mathModule2Easy.explanationEn:
1. Sum the data values: $6 + 8 + 16 + 4 + 17 + 26 + 8 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 100$.
2. Divide by the count ($n = 10$): $\text{Mean} = \frac{100}{10} = 10$. Choice B is correct.
mathModule2Easy.explanationUz:
1. Hamma sonlar yig'indisi: 100.
2. Sonlar soni: 10 ta. O'rtacha arifmetik: 100 / 10 = 10.
mathModule2Easy.desmosTrick: Type 'mean([6, 8, 16, 4, 17, 26, 8, 5, 5, 5])' in Desmos: outputs 10.

mathModule2Easy.prompt: Aubrey can run at a pace of 6 miles per hour. Running at the same rate, how many miles can she run in 90 minutes?
mathModule2Easy.explanationEn:
1. Convert 90 minutes to hours: $90\text{ minutes} = \frac{90}{60} = 1.5\text{ hours}$.
2. Distance = Rate × Time: $d = 6\text{ mph} \times 1.5\text{ hours} = 9\text{ miles}$. Source: SAT Math Practice Quiz.
mathModule2Easy.explanationUz:
1. 90 minutni soatga aylantiramiz: 90 / 60 = 1.5 soat.
2. Masofa = Tezlik * Vaqt: 6 * 1.5 = 9 mil.
mathModule2Easy.desmosTrick: Type '6 * (90/60)' into Desmos to get 9 immediately.

mathModule2Easy.prompt: A farmer can pick 12 cabbages in 1 hour. Working at the same rate, how long in hours would it take two farmers to pick 48 cabbages?
mathModule2Easy.explanationEn:
1. One farmer's rate = 12 cabbages/hour.
2. Two farmers working together produce $12 \times 2 = 24$ cabbages/hour.
3. Time required: $\frac{48\text{ cabbages}}{24\text{ cabbages/hour}} = 2\text{ hours}$.
mathModule2Easy.explanationUz:
1. 1 ta dehqon 1 soatda 12 ta karam teradi.
2. 2 ta dehqon 1 soatda 24 ta teradi.
3. 48 ta karam uchun: 48 / 24 = 2 soat.
mathModule2Easy.desmosTrick: Calculate 48 / (12 * 2) = 2.

mathModule2Easy.prompt: A digital tablet originally priced at $\$450$ is discounted by $20\%$. If a sales tax of $8\%$ is applied to the discounted price, what is the final purchase price?
mathModule2Easy.explanationEn:
1. Calculate discounted price:
$$\text{Discounted Price} = 450 \times (1 - 0.20) = 450 \times 0.80 = 360$$
2. Apply $8\%$ sales tax to the discounted price:
$$\text{Final Price} = 360 \times (1 + 0.08) = 360 \times 1.08 = 388.80$$
3. Correct Choice: B.
mathModule2Easy.explanationUz:
1. 20% chegirma: $450 \times 0.80 = 360$.
2. 8% soliq qo'shilishi: $360 \times 1.08 = 388.80$.
3. To'g'ri javob: B.
mathModule2Easy.desmosTrick: Desmosga: 450 * 0.8 * 1.08 deb kiriting -> 388.8 chiqadi.

mathModule2Easy.prompt: Which of the following expressions is equivalent to $32x^2 + 32$?
mathModule2Easy.explanationEn: 1. Factor out the greatest common factor (GCF), which is $32$: $32x^2 + 32 = 32(x^2 + 1)$. Option A is correct.
mathModule2Easy.explanationUz: 1. Umumiy ko'paytuvchi 32 ni qavsdan tashqariga chiqaramiz: 32(x^2 + 1).
mathModule2Easy.desmosTrick: Enter '32x^2 + 32' on line 1, and '32(x^2 + 1)' on line 2. Both curves overlap identically.

mathModule2Easy.prompt: The function $f$ is defined by $f(x) = 86(0.2)^x$. What is the value of $f(2)$?
mathModule2Easy.explanationEn:
1. Substitute $x = 2$ into the function: $f(2) = 86(0.2)^2$.
2. $(0.2)^2 = 0.04$.
3. Multiply: $86 \times 0.04 = 3.44$. Option A is correct.
mathModule2Easy.desmosTrick: Type '86(0.2)^2' directly into Desmos. It outputs 3.44 immediately.

mathModule2Easy.prompt: A high-speed train travels at a constant velocity of $60$ miles per hour. Given that $1\text{ mile} = 5{,}280\text{ feet}$ and $1\text{ hour} = 3{,}600\text{ seconds}$, what is the train's speed in feet per second?
mathModule2Easy.explanationEn:
1. Set up dimensional analysis unit conversion:
   $\frac{60\text{ miles}}{1\text{ hour}} \times \frac{5{,}280\text{ feet}}{1\text{ mile}} \times \frac{1\text{ hour}}{3{,}600\text{ seconds}}$.
2. Cancel units and compute:
   $\frac{60 \times 5280}{3600} = \frac{316{,}800}{3600} = 88\text{ ft/s}$.
mathModule2Easy.explanationUz: 1. Birliklar konvertatsiyasi: 60 * 5280 / 3600 = 88 fut/sekund.
mathModule2Easy.desmosTrick: Type '60 * 5280 / 3600' in Desmos to evaluate 88 instantly.

mathModule2Easy.prompt: Pump A can drain an industrial reservoir in $4\text{ hours}$, while Pump B can drain the same reservoir in $6\text{ hours}$. If both pumps operate simultaneously at their constant respective rates, how many hours will it take to drain the entire reservoir?
mathModule2Easy.explanationEn:
1. Combined rate formula: $\frac{1}{T} = \frac{1}{t_1} + \frac{1}{t_2}$.
2. $\frac{1}{T} = \frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{6} = \frac{3}{12} + \frac{2}{12} = \frac{5}{12}$.
3. Invert to find time: $T = \frac{12}{5} = 2.4\text{ hours}$. Choice A is correct.
mathModule2Easy.explanationUz:
1. Birgalikda ishlash formulasi: 1/T = 1/4 + 1/6 = 5/12.
2. T = 12 / 5 = 2.4 soat.
mathModule2Easy.desmosTrick: Type '1 / (1/4 + 1/6)' in Desmos: outputs 2.4.

mathModule2Easy.prompt: The price of a computer monitor was increased by $20\%$. Due to slow holiday sales, the new price was subsequently reduced by $20\%$. The final price is what percentage of the original price?
mathModule2Easy.explanationEn:
1. College Board Trap Alert: Increasing by 20% and then decreasing by 20% does NOT return to 100%!
2. Let original price be $P$.
3. After 20% increase: $P \times 1.20$.
4. After 20% decrease: $(1.20 P) \times (1 - 0.20) = 1.20 P \times 0.80 = 0.96 P$.
5. $0.96 = 96\%$ of original price (a net 4% decrease).
mathModule2Easy.explanationUz:
1. SAT Tuzog'i: 20% ga oshib, keyin 20% ga tushsa 100% bo'lmaydi!
2. 1.20 * 0.80 = 0.96 = 96% bo'ladi (4% arzonroq).
mathModule2Easy.desmosTrick: Enter '1.20 * 0.80' in Desmos to see 0.96 (96%).

mathModule2Easy.prompt: A car dealership has only sedans, SUVs, and minivans available for sale. On Monday, $20\%$ of the vehicles were sedans and $50\%$ were SUVs. If there were exactly $22$ sedans for sale on Monday, how many minivans were for sale?
mathModule2Easy.explanationEn:
1. The percentages of all vehicles must sum to $100\%$.
2. Percentage of minivans $= 100\% - (20\% + 50\%) = 30\%$.
3. We know $20\%$ corresponds to $22$ sedans: $0.20 \times \text{Total} = 22 \implies \text{Total} = \frac{22}{0.20} = 110$ vehicles.
4. Number of minivans $= 0.30 \times 110 = 33$. Choice C is correct.
mathModule2Easy.explanationUz:
1. Minivenlar ulushi: 100% - (20% + 50%) = 30%.
2. 20% bu 22 ta mashina bo'lsa, jami: 22 / 0.20 = 110 ta mashina.
3. Minivenlar soni: 110 ning 30% i = 33 ta.
mathModule2Easy.desmosTrick: Type '22 / 0.20 * 0.30' into Desmos to evaluate 33.

mathModule2Easy.prompt: After a store applied a $25\%$ promotional discount to the sticker price of a winter jacket, a buyer paid $\$135$ before taxes. What was the original sticker price of the jacket?
mathModule2Easy.explanationEn:
1. A $25\%$ discount means the buyer paid $100\% - 25\% = 75\%$ of the original price $P$.
2. Set up equation: $0.75 P = 135$.
3. Solve for $P$: $P = \frac{135}{0.75} = \frac{135}{3/4} = 135 \times \frac{4}{3} = 45 \times 4 = \$180$. Choice C is correct.
mathModule2Easy.explanationUz:
1. 25% chegirma degani asl narxning 75% i to'langan degani: 0.75 * P = 135.
2. P = 135 / 0.75 = 180 dollar.
mathModule2Easy.desmosTrick: Type '135 / 0.75' into Desmos to evaluate 180.

mathModule2Easy.prompt: A dataset of $15$ home prices has a mean of $\$320{,}000$ and a median of $\$315{,}000$. A luxury mansion priced at $\$3{,}500{,}000$ is added to the dataset. Which of the following statements best describes the effect of adding this value?
options: A) Both the mean and median will increase by approximately the same amount.
B) The mean will increase significantly, but the median will remain virtually unchanged.
C) The median will increase significantly, but the mean will remain unchanged.
D) Neither the mean nor the median will change.
mathModule2Easy.explanationEn:
1. An extreme high value is an outlier.
2. Outliers dramatically pull the arithmetic MEAN toward themselves because the sum increases enormously.
3. The MEDIAN is resistant to outliers because it only shifts over by one position in the ordered list. Thus, choice B is correct.
mathModule2Easy.explanationUz:
1. Juda katta qiymat (outlier) o'rtacha arifmetik (MEAN) ni keskin oshiradi.
2. MEDIAN esa tartiblangan ro'yxatda faqat bitta o'rin siljiydi, shuning uchun deyarli o'zgarmaydi.
mathModule2Easy.desmosTrick: Outliers heavily skew the mean, but have minimal or zero impact on the median.

mathModule2Easy.prompt: In a summary box plot representing the test scores of $80$ students, the first quartile ($Q_1$) is $68$ and the third quartile ($Q_3$) is $86$. What is the interquartile range (IQR) of the scores?
mathModule2Easy.explanationEn:
1. Recall the definition: $\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1$.
2. $\text{IQR} = 86 - 68 = 18$. Choice B is correct.
mathModule2Easy.explanationUz: 1. IQR (Kvartillararo masofa) = Q3 - Q1 = 86 - 68 = 18.

mathModule2Easy.skill: Two-Variable Data: Scatterplots & Line of Best Fit
mathModule2Easy.prompt: A scatterplot displays the relationship between weekly hours of tutoring ($x$) and score increase on a standardized test ($y$). The equation of the line of best fit is $\hat{y} = 3.6x + 14.5$. According to this model, what is the predicted score increase for a student who completes $8$ hours of tutoring?
mathModule2Easy.explanationEn:
1. Substitute $x = 8$ into the linear model: $\hat{y} = 3.6(8) + 14.5$.
2. Compute: $3.6 \times 8 = 28.8$.
3. Add intercept: $28.8 + 14.5 = 43.3$. Option C is correct.
mathModule2Easy.explanationUz: 1. x = 8 ni regressiya tenglamasiga qo'yamiz: 3.6(8) + 14.5 = 28.8 + 14.5 = 43.3.
mathModule2Easy.desmosTrick: Type '3.6 * 8 + 14.5' in Desmos to evaluate 43.3.

mathModule2Easy.prompt: An electronic tablet originally listed for price $P$ was discounted by $20\%$. During a weekend flash sale, the discounted price was reduced by an additional $15\%$. What was the total overall percentage discount from the original list price?
mathModule2Easy.explanationEn:
1. **Classic Trap Alert**: Do NOT add the percentages ($20\% + 15\% = 35\%$ is incorrect!). Successive discounts compound on the reduced price.
2. Method 1 (Assume Base 100): Start with an original price of $\$100$.
   - First discount of $20\%$: $100 \times (1 - 0.20) = \$80$.
   - Second discount of $15\%$: $80 \times (1 - 0.15) = 80 \times 0.85 = \$68$.
3. The final price is $\$68$. Overall savings: $100 - 68 = \$32$, which is an overall discount of $32\%$.
4. Multiplier formula: Overall factor $= (1 - 0.20)(1 - 0.15) = (0.80)(0.85) = 0.68$. Discount $= 1 - 0.68 = 0.32 = 32\%$.
mathModule2Easy.explanationUz:
1. SAT klassik tuzog'i: 20% + 15% = 35% deb qo'shib bo'lmaydi.
2. Boshlang'ich narxni 100 deb olamiz: 100 * 0.80 = 80 dollar. 80 * 0.85 = 68 dollar.
3. 100 - 68 = 32% umumiy chegirma!
mathModule2Easy.desmosTrick: Enter '1 - (0.80 * 0.85)' in Desmos. It outputs 0.32, which is 32%!

mathModule2Easy.prompt: If the expression $\frac{2x^2 + 7x - 5}{x + 3}$ is rewritten in the equivalent form $q(x) + \frac{r}{x + 3}$, where $q(x)$ is a polynomial and $r$ is a constant, what is the value of $r$?
mathModule2Easy.explanationEn:
1. By the Remainder Theorem, the remainder $r$ when $P(x) = 2x^2 + 7x - 5$ is divided by $(x + 3)$ is simply $P(-3)$.
2. Substitute $x = -3$: $P(-3) = 2(-3)^2 + 7(-3) - 5 = 2(9) - 21 - 5 = 18 - 26 = -8$.
3. Therefore, $r = -8$. Option A is correct.
mathModule2Easy.explanationUz:
1. Qoldiq haqidagi teoremaga ko'ra, x + 3 ga bo'lgandagi qoldiq r = P(-3) bo'ladi.
2. P(-3) = 2(-3)^2 + 7(-3) - 5 = 18 - 21 - 5 = -8.

mathModule2Easy.prompt: Which of the following is equivalent to the complex fraction $\frac{5 + 2i}{3 - 4i}$, where $i = \sqrt{-1}$?
mathModule2Easy.explanationEn:
1. Multiply numerator and denominator by the complex conjugate of denominator ($3 + 4i$):
   $\frac{(5 + 2i)(3 + 4i)}{(3 - 4i)(3 + 4i)}$.
2. Denominator: $3^2 - (4i)^2 = 9 - 16(-1) = 9 + 16 = 25$.
3. Numerator: $(5)(3) + 5(4i) + 2i(3) + 2i(4i) = 15 + 20i + 6i + 8(-1) = (15 - 8) + 26i = 7 + 26i$.
4. Combine: $\frac{7 + 26i}{25} = \frac{7}{25} + \frac{26}{25}i$. Choice A is correct.
mathModule2Easy.explanationUz:
1. Maxrajning qo'shmasi (3 + 4i) ga ko'paytiramiz.
2. Maxraj: 3^2 + 4^2 = 25.
3. Surat: (5 + 2i)(3 + 4i) = 15 + 20i + 6i - 8 = 7 + 26i.
4. Natija: 7/25 + 26/25 i.
mathModule2Easy.desmosTrick: Multiply by conjugate: (5*3 - 2*4) = 7, (5*4 + 2*3) = 26, denominator = 3^2 + 4^2 = 25. Thus (7 + 26i)/25.

rwModule1.prompt:
Scientists have long believed that giraffes are mostly silent and communicate only visually with one another. But biologist
Angela Stöger and her team analyzed hundreds of hours of recordings of giraffes in three European zoos and found that
giraffes make a very low-pitched humming sound. The researchers claim that the giraffes use these sounds to communicate
when it’s not possible for them to signal one another visually.
Which finding, if true, would most directly support Stöger and her team’s claim?
options: A) Giraffes have an excellent sense of vision and can see in color.
B) The giraffes only produced the humming sounds at night when they couldn’t see one another.
C) Wild giraffes have never been recorded making humming sounds.
D) Researchers observed other animals in European zoos humming.
rwModule1.explanationEn:
Choice B is the best answer because it presents a nding that, if true, would support Stöger and her team’s claim
that giraffes use humming to communicate when they cannot signal to one another visually. The text indicates that
scientists have long thought that giraffes produce little sound and exclusively rely on visual signals to
communicate with one another. The text goes on to say, however, that Stöger and her team have recorded giraffes in
three European zoos making a low-pitched humming sound, which the team claims the giraffes use to
communicate when they cannot see each other. If the giraffes produced these sounds when visual communication
was impossible and never produced them otherwise, that would support Stöger and her team’s claim about the
circumstance in which giraffes make the sound.
Choice A is incorrect because nding that giraffes have excellent vision and can see in color would have no bearing
on Stöger and her team’s claim that giraffes produce a low-pitched humming noise to communicate when they
cannot communicate visually. As presented in the text, Stöger and her team’s claim is restricted to circumstances in
which giraffes cannot signal one another visually; if the giraffes are unable to signal visually, their sense of vision is
irrelevant to their communication. Choice C is incorrect because nding that wild giraffes have never been recorded
making humming noises would not support Stöger and her team’s claim about the function of the humming noise
that the researchers recorded from the giraffes in European zoos. The text provides no information about whether
researchers have even attempted to record low-pitched humming in wild giraffes, so nothing can be concluded
about the implications of the lack of such recordings. Choice D is incorrect because nding that other animals in
European zoos had been observed humming would not support Stöger and her team’s claim, since it would not
indicate anything about why giraffes produce humming sounds. Different species could produce similar sounds for




different purposes, so scientists could not conclude anything about the function of giraffe humming from a nding
that some other animals in zoos also hum.

rwModule1.prompt:
In her 2021 article “Throwaway History: Towards a Historiography of Ephemera,” scholar Anne Garner discusses John
Johnson (1882–1956), a devoted collector of items intended to be discarded, including bus tickets and campaign
pamphlets. Johnson recognized that scholarly institutions considered his expansive collection of ephemera to be worthless
—indeed, it wasn’t until 1968, after Johnson’s death, that Oxford University’s Bodleian Library acquired the collection, having
grasped the items’ potential value to historians and other researchers. Hence, the example of Johnson serves to ______

options:
A) demonstrate the difficulties faced by contemporary historians in conducting research at the Bodleian Library without
access to ephemera.

institutions.

Choice A is incorrect. This inference isn’t supported. The text tells us that the Bodleian Library acquired Johnson’s
large collection of ephemera back in 1968, so we can assume that contemporary historians conducting research
there do have access to that collection. Choice B is incorrect. This inference isn’t supported. The text tells us that
“Oxford University’s Bodleian Library acquired the collection,” but it never suggests that it was a challenge to do so.
Choice C is incorrect. This inference isn’t supported. The text actually suggests the opposite: the example of

protection. Many ecologists have assumed that domed nests would provide protection from weather conditions and thus
would allow species that build them to have larger geographic ranges than species that build open nests do. To evaluate this
assumption, a research team led by evolutionary biologist Iliana Medina analyzed data for over 3,000 species of songbirds.

weather conditions, songbird species that build such nests should be able to have larger geographic ranges than

Choice A is incorrect because nothing in the text suggests that there’s a relationship between songbird species’
